statement: Let $f(x)=\\dfrac{ax+b}{cx+d}$ where $ad-bc\\neq0$. Find the condition on $a,b,c,d$ under which $f(f(x))=x$ for all $x$ for which both sides are defined. Hence describe the resulting family of functions.
solution: We compute $f(f(x))=\\dfrac{a\\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}+b}{c\\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}+d}=\\dfrac{a(ax+b)+b(cx+d)}{c(ax+b)+d(cx+d)}=\\dfrac{(a^{2}+bc)x+b(a+d)}{c(a+d)x+(bc+d^{2})}$. For this to equal $x$ identically we need $(a^{2}+bc)x+b(a+d)=c(a+d)x^{2}+(bc+d^{2})x$. Comparing coefficients gives $c(a+d)=0$, $b(a+d)=0$ and $a^{2}=d^{2}$. If $a+d\\neq0$ then $b=c=0$ and $a^{2}=d^{2}$; with $ad\\neq0$ this forces $a=-d$, giving $f(x)=-x$. If $a+d=0$ then $d=-a$ and $a^{2}=d^{2}$ holds automatically, with the only remaining requirement $ad-bc=-a^{2}-bc\\neq0$. Thus the non-trivial family is $f(x)=\\dfrac{ax+b}{cx-a}$ with $a^{2}+bc\\neq0$ (these are exactly the self-inverse Mobius maps, together with the trivial cases $f(x)=x$ and $f(x)=-x$).
hints: Compose f with itself and simplify the double fraction.
Compare coefficients of x^2, x and the constant term.
Two cases arise: a+d=0 or b=c=0.
